notes: Loop 2 (was 7.5). Rebuilt the demo by hand on net prices: €9.90 ÷ 1.106 − €3.60 = €5.35; lunch €6.54; 11.4 × €1.19 = €13.57; staff 1 h × €18 + €5 = €23; break-even 54.57 ÷ 5.35 = 10.2 → 11 (ongoing 7); scenarios −€385.20 / −€117.70 / +€256.80; worst −€545.70 (€862 if all switch); tornado 642/223.5/209.5/180.9; flat white €2.33/€2.58, −9.7%, rule 560/530. All right; every maths line reproduces, in German too ("9,90 €", "22.481,20 €"). Since loop 1: one decision rule (decision.ts) with grid tests showing verdict = card; a sum checker (engine.test.ts:228, :396); an honest worst case; cash kept apart from switching; the edge cases fixed; seeded property tests; German parsing with a read-back note. €13.90/€14.60 and the 7% food rate are right. Capped at 5 (§4, a wrong public fact): the drinks fact and the flat-white notes say milk drinks with at least 75% milk are 7% "since 1 January 2026". Drunk in the café, they are taxed at 19%. Only take-away is 7%, an older rule under Anlage 2. Following the note overstates a flat white's margin by about €0.39. Without the cap: about 8.4.
improvements: Wrong public fact (hard cap, §4). src/engine/messages.ts:147 (f.price.vat_rate.ask), :167 (note.vatPrice), :206 (fact.vat_drinks_19.label) and :489 (price.q.vat), the same keys in messages.de.ts:130/149/187/480 and in es/pl, plus site/src/messages.ts:97 (b.vat) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:141. All of them say milk drinks with at least 75% milk are taxed at 7%, and note.vatPrice says 'Since 1 January 2026 … if that is your item, change it to 7%'. In law, §12 Abs. 2 Nr. 15 UStG excludes 'die Abgabe von Getränken': every drink drunk on the premises is taxed at 19%. Only milk drinks sold to take away or delivered are 7% (§12 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 with Anlage 2; not plant milk), and that rule did not start in 2026. Rewrite it as 'Drinks: 19%, milk drinks drunk in the café included. To take away, milk drinks with at least 75% cow's milk: 7%.' Change the note to 'use 7% only for the take-away share; ask your Steuerberater'. Better still, give take-away milk drinks a fact of their own with the right legal basis. Criterion: correctness and source tags. Done when report-static.de.html's facts card and the flat-white note never offer 7% for a drink drunk in the café, and a test asserts that every catalog's milk-drink sentence names take-away.

The facts' links and legal basis. src/engine/berlin.ts:27-30 links the VAT facts to https://www.bundesfinanzministerium.de and the wage facts to https://www.bundesregierung.de, both home pages, and engine.test.ts:1065 pins exactly that. The owner (or her Steuerberater) cannot check a fact there. Link the documents themselves: §12 UStG at gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__12.html, or BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 363 (Steueränderungsgesetz 2025), and the MiLoV5 at gesetze-im-internet.de/milov5/. The 10.6% fallback rests on the BMF letter of 22 Dec 2025 (a flat 30% drinks share for combined offers), but that letter is not a fact: add it with its date and link, so the guess shows what it stands on. Done when every PublicFact.url has a path that opens the cited text and the test checks the path, not the domain.

The shipped price demo asks a wage question the maths never answers. src/report/demo.ts:59-104 and :179-183 ask 'What if I put my flat white up by 20 cents when the minimum wage rises from €13.90 to €14.60 on 1 January 2027?'. Yet price_change has no labour cost, and analysis.facts for that demo lists only the two VAT rates. So the €13.90 and €14.60 in the headline have no source in the facts card, and the result ('+€87 over the test') compares with today's margin, not with 2027 costs. Either add an optional staff_hours_per_week to price_change, have the engine compute the weekly cost of the rise (hours × €0.70) against the extra €0.17 net per cup × cups sold, and list min_wage_2026 and min_wage_2027 in facts (factsUsed, index.ts:93), or drop the wage from the demo question. Criterion: transparency and honesty. Done when the demo's facts card lists the minimum wage and one maths line says whether the 20 cents cover the rise.

Missing plausibility warnings. (a) A staff_hourly_cost below the legal minimum is taken without comment: €10 an hour gives a smaller break-even (9 instead of 11) and a cheaper test card. Warn in lunch-offer.ts near :556 when staffRate < MIN_WAGE_2026 (or MIN_WAGE_2027 for a test after 1 Jan 2027): 'below the legal minimum wage of €13.90 (since 1 Jan 2026), and employer contributions come on top'. (b) With lunch_customers 0, lunch.warn.gap (lunch-offer.ts:571) still says 'every regular who switches costs you money'. Gate it on m.switchers > 0. Criterion: edge cases. Done when named tests cover both.

Words that do not match the number they describe. (a) plan.lunch.capSwitch and plan.lunch.measure.regulars.how say switching regulars 'lower your takings by about €13.57 a day … strokes × €1.19'. €1.19 is the margin after VAT, but the till (Z-Bon) shows €1.30 less per switcher (11.4 × €1.30 = €14.82). Say 'lower what you keep'. (b) weekday_left_month (lunch-offer.ts:340) applies the 10.6% lunch blend to all weekday takings, which are mostly drinks at 19%; say so in the maths line or use 19% there. (c) In explainPriceChange, a VAT change prints 'you can now lose up to 9.7% of sales (60 a week) instead of 9.7% (60)'; print 'break-even stays at −9.7%' instead. (d) In German, 'was die Kasse zeigt, vor Mehrwertsteuer und Kosten' reads as 'net'; write 'mit Mehrwertsteuer, vor Kosten'. Criterion: transparency.

Code: one source of truth for language and currency. format.ts:14-22 still holds the currency as mutable module state. analyze (index.ts:108-110), planTest (experiment.ts:21-22) and compareResult (compare.ts:198-199) set the language and currency as side effects. src/report/sections.ts:445-456 keeps fallback money arithmetic (p.netTest − gp.netTest, perTest ÷ days, dx × per × days), although the engine now always sends vsGuess and perStep. Pass lang and currency explicitly, and delete the report-side fallbacks so that no money is worked out outside src/engine. Criterion: code a reviewer can follow.
